title: RabbitMQ Ack Windows, Broker Restart, and a Poison Message
objective: Run RabbitMQ with durable queues and compare four named failure points — crash before ack, crash after side-effect, broker restart while a message is unacked, and a poison message that never succeeds — then write a table that states the actual delivery guarantee for each row against the Kafka offset-commit window from ds1t2-002 / ds1t2-003.
whyThisMatters: The SWE RabbitMQ task asks for retries, a DLQ, and an idempotent consumer. That is the happy path of reliability. This task times the ack against the side-effect and against a broker restart, then puts Kafka's offset commit next to it, so 'at-least-once' is a set of windows you measured rather than a slogan both brokers share.
evidence: Compose (or equivalent) for RabbitMQ and git history showing durable topology before the four failure runs

A results table (Markdown or CSV) with four rows: crash-before-ack, crash-after-side-effect, broker-restart-unacked, poison — each with predicted outcome, actual outcome, and whether the domain effect ran 0, 1, or N times
Captured broker/consumer logs for the poison path showing the message on a dead-letter queue after a bounded retry count you configured
README stating prefetch, ack mode, retry limit, and the actual guarantee (never 'exactly-once')
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: All four failure classes are run against a durable queue and a durable published message; the table has a predicted column committed or timestamped before the corresponding run.
Crash-after-side-effect shows the domain effect occurring more than once unless an idempotency key suppresses the second apply — and the table says which of those two you implemented.
The poison message appears on an inspectable dead-letter queue after at most the configured retry count, and that count is a number in README and in the broker policy or application retry loop.

README compares each of the four rows to the equivalent Kafka failure (offset commit before vs after the side-effect, broker loss of an uncommitted produce) in one sentence per row — not a brand preference.
